## Investigation of `region.fasta`

**Method:** the 3,000 bp record `region_001` was analyzed for base composition, repeats, restriction sites, all six reading frames (stop-codon-free stretches, start/stop-codon-defined ORFs, translations, motif searches, and antisense-frame checks). No homology/database search was available, so functional assignment rests on internal sequence motifs.

### 1. Overall properties
| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Length | 3,000 bp |
| G+C | 50.9 % (A 725, C 802, G 725, T 748) |
| Repeats | none ≥ 20 bp; no tandem/periodic repeats of note |
| Restriction sites | only single BamHI (1197–1202) and SphI (137–142) sites; no site clusters |
| Long inverted repeats | exactly one (a 26-bp perfect hairpin, see §4) |
| GC skew (500-bp windows) | mildly negative (−0.04 to −0.11) everywhere except the last window (+0.07) |

The sequence is **not** random: it is a **gene-dense, single-strand-encoded fragment of a larger (prokaryote-like) genome**. The very first position falls inside a coding sequence, so all coordinates below are relative to this 3-kb fragment.

### 2. Genes — all four are on the **minus** strand
All coordinates are 1-based on the plus strand of the file; each gene is read right-to-left (transcription start at the high coordinate).

### 3. The notable feature: gene A is a class I aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase
The 428-aa product of gene A contains the diagnostic catalytic motifs of the **class I aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases** (positions given as protein residue / plus-strand coordinate of the codon):

* **HIGH-type motif**, `HLGH`, residues 52–55 → **1787–1798**
* **Class I "motif 3" peptide**, `SDQWGN` (part of `GSDQWGNITS`), residues 203–208 → **1328–1345**
* **KMSKS-type lysine-rich loop**, `KFGK…TEGG` (Lys239–Gly242 within `ITKADGTKFGKTEGG`), residues 239–242 → **1226–1237**
* Glycine-rich Rossmann ATP-binding loop, `VGGATGLIGDP` (residues ~75–85)
* C-terminal `C…C` (`CLIC`) at residues 423–426 → 674–685

Product: `MEILMASSNLIKQLQERGLVAQVTDEEALAERLAQGPIALYCGFDPTADSLHLGHLVPLLCLKR…`
This motif signature is unambiguous — the region encodes a **class I tRNA-charging enzyme** (fragment of a housekeeping gene cluster). Its size (428 aa, i.e. the core catalytic domain plus the C-terminal tRNA-binding domain, with no large editing-domain insertion) and the `KFGK` variant of the KMSKS loop are most consistent with a **tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase (TyrRS)**-type enzyme; a cysteinyl- or tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase relationship cannot be formally excluded without a database search. Genes B, C and D show no diagnostic motifs and remain functionally unassigned.

### 4. Other features worth noting
**Candidate rho-independent transcription terminator, 618–650 (+ strand coords), in the 58-bp spacer between genes A and B.**
* GC-rich 11-bp stem: `AGGGGGAGTGA` (625–635) paired with `TCACTCCCCCT` (640–650)
* 4-nt loop `TTTC` (636–639)
* followed, in the minus-strand (gene A) transcript, by a U-rich tract `UUUUU` (5′-end of the transcript corresponds to plus-strand `AAAAA` at 618–622)
So the arrangement `[stem–loop][U5]` is textbook, and it sits just downstream of the stop codon (665–667) of gene A — consistent with gene A being transcribed as its own unit.

**A cautionary result (why nothing else on the plus strand is a gene).** The plus strand shows long apparent ORFs, e.g. **1004–1774 (256 aa)** and **1963–2517 (184 aa)**, which would look like genes. They are artifacts: every one of them lies in the exact antisense register of a minus-strand gene, and for each plus-strand stop codon inside gene A (plus positions **710, 989, 1772, 1865**) the corresponding minus-strand codon is **TTA**, i.e. a Leu codon whose reverse complement is a stop. Because the antisense register of any coding sequence is stop-free except at TTA/CTA/TCA codons, it generates spurious long ORFs "for free". Their translations (`MQTTGQVDTR…`, etc.) show no resemblance to any known protein. Similarly, the plus-strand ORFs 58–369 and 430–660 are antisense artifacts of gene B. The remaining short plus-strand ORFs (219–482, 87 aa; 2205–2429, 74 aa; 2689–2922, 77 aa) are in frames unrelated to the minus-strand genes but are within the length range expected from chance, so they are at best speculative.

### Summary
`region.fasta` is a 3-kb fragment of a bacterial-style genome with ~92 % coding density. Its standout feature is **gene A (668–1951 on the minus strand, 428 aa), a class I aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase** (HIGH at 1787–1798, SDQWGN at 1328–1345, KFGKT at 1226–1237), flanked by three unassigned coding sequences read on the same strand (1–606, truncated; 2071–2724; 2786–2989) and a strong candidate rho-independent terminator at 618–650. There are no repeats or other unusual sequence features, and none of the plus-strand ORFs should be annotated as genes.
